description: This case study is the IAEA Director General's report on the Fukushima Daiichi accident, a 222-page assessment of the causes and consequences of the accident that began at the Japanese nuclear power plant on 11 March 2011 when a tsunami followed a large earthquake. The foreword calls it the worst accident at a nuclear power plant since Chernobyl in 1986, and the report examines human, organisational and technical factors together with the measures taken in Japan and internationally. It comes with five technical volumes on the description and context of the accident, safety assessment, emergency preparedness and response, radiological consequences and post-accident recovery, prepared with about 180 experts from 42 member states. Access: free PDFs on the IAEA publications server; the main publication page blocked the cloud session, and no licence is stated in the text. Coverage is one site and the international response. Caveats: only the front matter and foreword were read, and the technical volumes were not opened. It suits emergency response and resilience studies of nuclear plants under earthquake and tsunami hazards, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
